findings.title: Call to non-existent zero-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.java line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The only definition in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring one argument. There is no zero-arg overload. The code cannot compile, breaking the whole services module. It should pass the user, e.g. isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

findings.title: Passkeys conditional UI now requires a known user, disabling it on initial login
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) returns webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null. It is used in authenticate() and challenge() to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context). Previously the code filled the form when passkeys were enabled and context.getUser() == null (initial login). Now it only fills when context.getUser() != null (re-authentication). Initial login with no user therefore never gets ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, challenge, RP ID or webauth form, breaking username-less / conditional-UI passkey login. The PR's own tests still expect //form[@id='webauth'] on the first page.

findings.title: Re-authentication attributes set on throwaway form instance are lost
findings.body: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError() does LoginFormsProvider form = context.form(); form.setAttribute(USERNAME_HIDDEN,true); form.setAttribute(REGISTRATION_DISABLED,true); and then returns. The caller in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler() and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse() then creates a different instance via challenge()/errorChallenge.apply() which internally calls context.form() again. Each context.form() returns a new LoginFormsProvider, so attributes set on the first instance never reach the rendered response. After a failed password/passkey during re-authentication the page will show the regular login with editable username and registration link instead of hidden-username re-authentication.

findings.title: Error response discards webauthn form state via multiple context.form() instances
findings.body: createErrorResponse() calls context.form().setError(...), context.form().setAttribute(...), AuthenticatorUtils.setup...(context) which uses another context.form(), fillContextForm(context) whose returned LoginFormsProvider with new challenge and attributes is discarded, then return errorChallenge.apply(context) which builds yet another fresh form. Because each context.form() is a new instance, the error, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI flag, and the fresh challenge/attributes never make it into the returned Response. On passkey failure the user gets a page without the error displayed and without valid conditional-UI data, and the auth-session challenge note does not match what was rendered.
